newsitem.title: BELGIUM: FOCUS - Odds improve on EU yes to Anglo/Lonrho deal.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Odds improve on EU yes to Anglo/Lonrho deal.

text.p: The odds improved on Tuesday that Anglo-American Corp of South Africa will get EU approval for its stake in Lonrho with EU Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert saying a solution to the competition problems it raised was being sought.
"They know the problem, they are willing to discuss it," Van Miert told Reuters after speaking on competition issues at a lunch organised by the American Chamber of Commerce.

In April, the Commission blocked plans to merge the platinum interests of Britain's Lonrho and South African mining group Gencor, warning Anglo at the time there would be problems is it tried to take control of Lonrho.

Earlier this month Anglo-American increased its shareholding in Lonrho to 28 percent, effectively taking control of the industrial holding company whose operations include platinum mining and refining.
The deal was submitted to the European Commission which is the clearing house for large mergers and acquisitions affecting trade in the European Union.
Van Miert declined to say what sort of changes or commitments the companies would have to make with to get EU approval.

"I know they are seriously thinking about it but I cannot be more precise at this stage of the proceedings," he said, stressing that it was for the companies to suggest a remedy to avoid competition in the EU being harmed.
Anglo-American said in Johannesbourg it believed it could work out a deal with the EU.
"I am confident that we will be able to come to a satisfactory arrangement with the European Union," chairman Julian Ogilvie Thompson said.
He said Anglo would not control Lonrho's platinum business.
"We've always realised that in acquiring Lonrho (we would encounter difficulties with acquiring their platinum interests). We have no intention of doing that," he said.
"Amplats (Anglo American Platinum Corp of South Africa Ltd) is quite capable of competing with Lonrho Platinum".

The Commission must decide by mid December whether to clear Anglo's stake in Lonrho after its preliminary one-month review of the operation or start an in-depth probe that could last up to four months.
Van Miert said it was too early to tell whether the Commission would need that extra time.

Anglo is the world's largest producer of platinum with 35 percent of total output, the Commission said in April. Together with Lonrho and Gencor it controls 90 percent of the world reserves of platinum, a precious metal used particularly in jewellery and in making car catalytic converters
